title: 5 must-watch movies & TV shows streaming right now
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: 'The Devil Wears Prada 2', starring Meryl Streep and Anne Hathaway, is now streaming on Hulu.
'The Drama', a dark comedy featuring Zendaya and Robert Pattinson, is available on HBO Max.
'Furious' Season 1, a new series from Elizabeth Meriwether, is streaming on Hulu.

title: Here’s how home, away broadcasts reacted to Jarren Duran’s on-field flare-up
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Jarren Duran stirred controversy by appearing to call out teammate Willson Contreras and coach Chad Epperson during a game.
NESN and WEEI broadcasts expressed confusion and criticism over Duran's public outburst on the field.
Red Sox may trade Duran before Monday's deadline, despite team's recent success and his uncertain clubhouse dynamics.

title: Drake Maye on building chemistry with A.J. Brown: ‘I am not going to shy away from him.’
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Drake Maye and A.J. Brown are building chemistry during Patriots training camp, connecting frequently during team drills.
Brown's performance has improved since practices in pads began, highlighted by successful passes from Maye in recent sessions.
Maye emphasizes consistent communication and involving Brown in plays, enhancing their understanding and effectiveness on the field.

title: Drake Maye, A.J. Brown heat up and other takeaways from Day 6 of Patriots training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Drake Maye went 11-for-11 in 11-on-11 drills, showing improved chemistry with A.J. Brown at Patriots training camp.
Romeo Doubs impressed with a standout touchdown catch against top-tier cornerback Christian Gonzalez during Friday's practice.
Attendance issues continue as several Patriots, including Carlton Davis III and Christian Barmore, missed practice due to various reasons.

title: Massachusetts falls out of top 10 in best state rankings by U.S. News & World Report
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Massachusetts dropped to No. 11 in U.S. News & World Report's 2026 Best States rankings, falling from No. 9 in 2025.
Maintaining strong healthcare scores, Massachusetts ranked second overall but slipped in education and infrastructure standings.
Weak rankings in fiscal stability and opportunity contributed to Massachusetts' drop from the top 10 states.

title: Massachusetts loses two IHOP restaurants
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: IHOP closed its Cambridge and Hyannis locations, leaving 19 remaining franchise restaurants in Massachusetts.
The closures might be due to insufficient foot traffic or expired leases, not affecting other locations statewide.
Dine Brands Global, owner of IHOP, has 1,812 franchised locations and plans to add 245 more in seven years.

title: Court agrees Wu did not discriminate against North End restaurants, but may have illegally taxed them
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: A federal appeals court upheld the dismissal of a lawsuit against Boston's outdoor dining regulations affecting North End restaurants.
The court rejected claims that Mayor Wu's administration discriminated against North End restaurant owners due to their Italian heritage.
The appeals court left open the possibility of challenging the $7,500 impact fee as an unlawful tax.

title: MassDOT releases rendering of two new bridges along McGrath Highway
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: MassDOT plans to replace Squires Bridge and add a new bridge on McGrath Highway, affecting the Somerville/Cambridge area.
The Squires Bridge will be a 300-foot, single-span bridge with improved roadways and bike lanes, enhancing connectivity.
Construction to begin in 2030, with completion expected in three to four years; public feedback is being accepted.

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ review: Peter Parker grows up in emotionally mature sequel
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' stars Tom Holland and explores a more mature Peter Parker facing internal struggles.
The film features a somber New York City with action sequences and a unique faceless villain targeting Damage Control.
Zendaya's character MJ gains depth in this installment, showcasing her chemistry with Holland, her real-life husband.

title: This Boston law firm is boosting starting salaries to $235,000
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: McDermott Will & Schulte LLP raises starting salaries to $235,000 for first-year associates, effective July 1.
The salary increase aligns McDermott with top U.S. law firms, like Milbank, which recently set similar pay levels.
Major Boston firms have not matched McDermott's salary increase, with Ropes & Gray listing $225,000 for first-year associates.
